title: opstruss.yaml
description: An OpsTruss project, or a component when used through uses:.

name.description: The name of the project: lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.

opstruss.description: The oldest OpsTruss version that reads this file, as MAJOR.MINOR.

include.description: Files merged into the project, as globs relative to this file.

uses.description: Plugins, components, and catalogs that the project uses, by the name it calls them.

inputs.description: Inputs of the project, which stacks, --input, or a prompt give.

locals.description: Named values computed from inputs and other locals, read as locals.<name>.

outputs.description: Outputs of the project, which opstruss outputs prints and a project that uses it as a component reads.

stacks.description: The stacks of the project: copies of its units, each with its inputs and its own state.

backend.description: Where the state of the stacks is kept: local, in .opstruss/state/.

secrets.description: Secrets of the project, read as secrets.<name> and hidden in what OpsTruss writes.

encryption_keys.description: What opens the data key of each stack, which encrypts sensitive values in the state.

runtime.description: Settings of the daemon of each stack.

mcp.description: Reserved for opstruss mcp, which a later version brings: the tasks it offers to AI agents, or false for none.

units.description: The units of the project, which up brings up and destroy takes away.

tasks.description: The tasks of the project, each also a command of opstruss.

moved.description: Units that changed address, so that their records move rather than being destroyed.

removed.description: Units gone from the files, and whether destroy takes away what they made or their records are forgotten.

includeFile.description: A file merged into a project through include:.

name.description: A name: lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.

level.description: The OpsTruss version this file was written for, as MAJOR.MINOR.

globs.description: Paths or globs, relative to this file.

condition.description: A condition: an expression in ${{ }}, or true or false.

command.description: A program: a list of arguments, run as written, or a string, a script for shell.

env.description: Variables set for programs: a value, or {file: <value>} to write the value to a file and set the variable to its path.

file.description: The value, written to a file whose path the variable gets.

pass.description: Variables of the environment of OpsTruss that programs get, by name or by pattern such as AWS_*; never OPSTRUSS_ or INPUT_ ones.

requires.description: Programs that must be in PATH, or an expression that gives the list.

shell.description: The shell that runs a script: sh, bash, python, node, or pwsh; sh by default.

approval.description: ask to wait for approval of changes, auto to apply them without asking.

format.description: How a value is written as text: text, json, yaml, lines, or dotenv.

stdin.description: What a program reads on its standard input.

value.description: The value: text, or data that format writes.

format.description: How the value is written; text by default.

paths.description: Paths and globs relative to this file, read as written, without shell variables; {exclude: <glob>} leaves files out of those before it.

exclude.description: A glob of files to leave out of the patterns before it.

forEach.description: A list, a map, or an expression that gives one: one instance per item, read as each.key and each.value.

retry.description: Running a program again when it fails.

attempts.description: How many times the program runs at most, the first one included.

delay.description: The wait before the second attempt.

backoff.description: What each wait is multiplied by for the next one.

until.description: A condition on the outputs that ends the attempts when true.

stop.description: How a program is stopped, at cancel, timeout, or the end of a service.

signal.description: The signal that asks the program to stop; SIGINT by default, SIGTERM for a service.

grace.description: How long the program has after the signal before it is killed; 1m by default, 10s for a service.

run.description: A program that stops a service, instead of the signal.

input.description: An input: its type, its default, and the checks of its value.

description.description: What the input is for, which help shows.

required.description: Whether the input must be given.

default.description: The value when none is given.

env.description: A variable of the environment that gives the value; only in the files of a project.

pattern.description: A regular expression that a string must match.

items.description: What each item of an array is.

properties.description: The keys of an object, each one an input; other keys are refused.

sensitive.description: Hide the value in what OpsTruss writes, and keep it encrypted in the state.

args.description: Fill the array with the arguments after -- on the command line.

output.description: An output of a program or a task, and where its value comes from.

sensitive.description: Hide the value in what OpsTruss writes, and keep it encrypted in the state.

from.description: Where the value comes from: stdout, stderr, the file at path, or output, the lines name=value written to $OPSTRUSS_OUTPUT; output by default.

path.description: The file that from: file reads, relative to the directory of the program.

format.description: How the text is read: text, json, yaml, lines, or dotenv.

value.description: The value, as an expression of the steps of the task.

projectOutputs.description: Outputs of a project by name: an expression, or an object with value.

value.description: The value, as an expression of the outputs of units.

sensitive.description: Hide the value in what OpsTruss writes.

locals.description: Named values, each an expression, read as locals.<name>.

uses.description: What a project uses, by name: a source, or an object with source and what every use of it gets.

source.description: Where it comes from: a path, github.com/<owner>/<repo>[/<path>]@<ref>, <catalog>.<name>, or opstruss.<task> for a built-in task.

with.description: Inputs given to every use of it, under those of the use.

env.description: Variables set for its programs, under those of the use.

pass.description: Variables of the environment that its programs get when it asks for them, by name or pattern; not * alone, since the units that use it keep their values in their digest.

stack.description: A stack: a copy of the units of the project with its own inputs and state.

with.description: Values of the inputs of the project in this stack.

secrets.description: Secrets of this stack, over those of the project.

encryption_keys.description: What opens the data key of this stack, instead of those of the project.

runtime.description: Settings of the daemon of this stack.

mcp.description: Reserved for opstruss mcp: what it offers in this stack.

backend.description: Where the state of this stack is kept.

approval.description: ask to wait for approval of changes in this stack, auto to apply them without asking.

include.description: Files merged into the project in this stack only.

backend.description: Where the state of a stack is kept.

pass.description: Variables of the environment that the backend plugin gets.

secret.description: One source: sops, env, run, or a call of a plugin task whose output is value.

sops.description: A file encrypted with sops, relative to this file; a dotenv, JSON, or YAML file is a map.

field.description: One field of the decrypted file, as a dotted path.

env.description: The variable of the environment that holds the secret, or, with run:, variables for its program.

run.description: A program whose standard output is the secret, such as op read.

pass.description: Variables of the environment that the program of run: gets.

dir.description: The directory the program of run: starts in, relative to this file.

shell.description: The shell that runs run: when it is a script.

encryptionKeys.description: What opens the data key of each stack: age recipients (age1...), opened by OpsTruss, and keys that the sops program wraps it for.

gcp_kms.description: A Google Cloud KMS key resource ID.

azure_keyvault.description: An Azure Key Vault key URL.

hc_vault_transit_uri.description: A HashiCorp Vault transit key URI.

runtime.description: Settings of the daemon of a stack.

listen.description: The address where the daemon serves webhooks, as host:port; on: webhook needs it.

mcp.description: What opstruss mcp offers, or false for nothing.

tasks.description: The tasks that opstruss mcp offers as tools.

unit.description: A unit: something that up brings up and destroy takes away, with exactly one of run, service, or uses.

run.description: The program that brings the unit up.

service.description: A program that keeps running, which the daemon of the stack supervises.

uses.description: The plugin, task, or component that the unit uses.

with.description: Inputs of what the unit uses.

tasks.description: Tasks of the unit, run as opstruss <task> [unit]...

requires.description: Programs that must be in PATH before the unit runs.

shell.description: The shell that runs a script; sh by default.

dir.description: The directory that the programs start in, relative to this file.

env.description: Variables set for the programs of the unit.

pass.description: Variables of the environment that the programs of the unit get; not * alone, since the unit keeps their values in its digest and destroy context.

stdin.description: What the program reads on its standard input.

sources.description: Files whose content is part of the definition, so a change to one runs the unit again.

generates.description: Files that the unit makes, relative to this file and read as written; a missing one runs the unit again.

revision.description: A value whose change runs the unit again.

outputs.description: Outputs of the program, which other units read as units.<name>.outputs.<output>.

destroy.description: The program that takes the unit away, which its record keeps.

restart.description: When the daemon starts the service again after it exits: no, on-failure, or always; on-failure by default.

ready.description: When the service counts as started: a URL, a port, or a program; up waits for it.

http.description: A URL that answers with a 2xx status once the service is ready.

tcp.description: A host:port that accepts a connection once the service is ready.

run.description: A program that exits with 0 once the service is ready.

timeout.description: How long up waits for the service to be ready.

needs.description: Units that come before this one, besides those its expressions read.

if.description: A condition that decides whether the unit is in the stack; one that leaves it is destroyed.

for_each.description: A list or a map: one instance of the unit per item, read as each.key and each.value.

approval.description: ask to wait for approval of changes to this unit, auto to apply them without asking.

timeout.description: How long a program of the unit may run.

retry.description: Running the program again when it fails.

call.description: A call of a task by name, with its inputs.

task.description: Exactly one of run, steps, or one call of a task.

description.description: What the task does, which help and list show.

inputs.description: Inputs of the task, each also a flag of its command.

shell.description: The shell that runs a script, also for each step; sh by default.

dir.description: The directory that the programs start in, relative to this file, also for each step.

env.description: Variables set for the programs of the task and its steps.

pass.description: Variables of the environment that the programs of the task and its steps get.

stdin.description: What the program reads on its standard input.

requires.description: Programs that must be in PATH before the task runs.

needs.description: Tasks that run before this one.

if.description: A condition that skips the task when false.

for_each.description: A list or a map: the task runs once per item, read as each.key and each.value.

max_parallel.description: How many items of for_each run at once; OPSTRUSS_PARALLEL by default.

on.description: Triggers that run the task from the daemon of the stack.

approval.description: ask to wait for approval of the changes that the task makes, auto to apply them without asking.

concurrency.description: What a new run of the task does while another goes on, also across the tasks of one group.

group.description: A name that the tasks whose runs wait for one another share.

mode.description: What a new run does: queue, cancel, skip, or parallel; queue by default.

timeout.description: How long the task may run.

retry.description: Running the task again when it fails.

failed_when.description: A condition on the outputs that marks the task failed.

changed_when.description: A condition on the outputs that says whether the task changed something.

continue_on_error.description: Record a failure and go on.

internal.description: Leave the task out of the commands and the MCP tools; other tasks and its own on: still run it.

concurrencyMode.description: What a new run does while another run of the task goes on: queue, cancel the other, skip, or run in parallel.

steps.description: Steps that run one after another.

step.description: Exactly one of run, task, block, or one call of a task.

name.description: The name that the output shows for the step.

id.description: The id that later steps read as steps.<id>.

if.description: A condition that skips the step when false.

task.description: A task of the project, or a standard task such as up, to run.

block.description: Steps that rescue and always go with.

rescue.description: Steps that run when a step of block fails, which then counts as handled.

always.description: Steps that run after block and rescue, whether they failed or not.

with.description: Inputs of the task of task:.

units.description: The units that task: up, destroy, status, or logs acts on.

yes.description: Approve the changes of task: up or destroy, as --yes does.

force.description: As --force for task: up or destroy.

pass.description: Variables of the environment that the program gets.

shell.description: The shell that runs a script.

dir.description: The directory that the program starts in, relative to this file.

stdin.description: What the program reads on its standard input.

timeout.description: How long the step may run.

for_each.description: A list or a map: the step runs once per item, read as each.key and each.value.

retry.description: Running the step again when it fails.

failed_when.description: A condition on the outputs that marks the step failed.

changed_when.description: A condition on the outputs that says whether the step changed something.

continue_on_error.description: Record a failure and go on with the next step.

outputs.description: Outputs of the program of the step.

triggers.description: What runs a task from the daemon of the stack.

schedule.description: Cron schedules, in the time zone of the machine unless timezone names another.

every.description: Intervals, such as 5m, from when the daemon starts.

webhook.description: HTTP requests to the daemon that run the task.

watch.description: Events from files, the output of a service, or a program that writes a line per event.

after.description: Runs of other tasks or commands that this task follows.

schedule.description: A cron schedule, as a string or with its options.

cron.description: A cron expression of five fields, or a shorthand such as @daily.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as Asia/Jakarta; the time zone of the machine by default.

persistent.description: Run once what was missed while the daemon was not running or the machine slept.

if.description: A condition on the event that skips the run when false.

with.description: Inputs of the task for runs of this trigger.

webhook.description: An HTTP request to the daemon that runs the task, checked by its signature.

path.description: The path that the daemon serves the webhook at.

method.description: The HTTP method; POST by default.

secret.description: The secret that signs the requests, as ${{ secrets.<name> }}.

signature.description: How a request is checked: the scheme of github, gitlab, slack, stripe, standard webhooks, or bearer, or a header of your own.

header.description: The header that holds the signature.

prefix.description: Text before the signature in the header, such as sha256=.

respond.description: accepted to answer 202 with the id of the run at once, or wait to answer with the outputs of the task.

if.description: A condition on the event that skips the run when false.

with.description: Inputs of the task for runs of this trigger.

watch.description: Exactly one source: unit, paths, or one call of a task.

unit.description: A service whose output lines are the events.

paths.description: Files to watch, relative to this file.

stream.description: Which output of the service: stdout, stderr, or both; both by default.

if.description: A condition on the event that skips the run when false.

batch.description: Gather the events of this long into one run.

debounce.description: Run once no event has come for this long.

with.description: Inputs of the task for runs of this trigger.

after.description: Running after a run of another task or command ends.

task.description: The task, or the command such as up, whose runs this task follows.

unit.description: Only runs that touched this unit.

outcome.description: Which runs: success, failure, or any; success by default.

if.description: A condition on the event that skips the run when false.

with.description: Inputs of the task for runs of this trigger.

moved.description: Addresses that changed, from the old to the new.

from.description: The address of the unit that left the files.

destroy.description: true to destroy what the unit made, false to forget its record and leave it.
